newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks end session quietly firmer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks end session quietly firmer.

text.p: SPI Futures cl 2325 +12 US 30yr 6.66 +0.03
10yrbond futs 92.450 +0.025 Gold NY 368.75 Lon fix 368.30
*Stocks ended a quiet session moderately firmer after the Dow bounced on Tuesday. Volume 349.6 million, value 807.7 million, 1,020 stocks traded, 303 steady, 417 up, 300 down.
Australian shares finished a quiet session modestly firmer on Wednesday with stocks holding onto early gains after Wall Street hinted that its recent rally was not yet complete on Tuesday.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 7.9 points higher at 2,323.7, not far from its intra-day high of 2,328.6.
December share price index futures ended 12 points firmer at 2,325, a 1.3 point premium to the underlying index.
Turnover was steady during the session with key buying interest in cyclical stocks like building materials, transport and media as well as for a handful of base metal miners.
"It was a mixed bag. There were a few standout stocks like Lend Lease and News Corp but without much news people were just buying on the back of the Dow," a Sydney-based dealer said.
The dealer said the level of turnover was encouraging and suggested that investors were reasonably confident that Wall Street could continue to run higher in the lead-up to Christmas.
"It would take some dire news to send the market into a spin. I think most traders are comfortable to hold stock, particularly after last week's rate cut," the dealer said.
Beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil continued to be singled out for selling attention a month after its profit downgrade.
Dealers said market direction was likely to be strongly linked to the fortunes of Wall Street for at least the next month with little local news seen impacting day to day trade.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about four to three, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures and options trade was moderate with options business most active in major resource issues BHP and WMC.
Total options traded 36,527 (31,880)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 6,272 (7,706)

In other local markets, Australian bonds held steady just in positive territory through a quiet afternoon session after earlier pared opening losses in a reasonably busy morning session, traders said.
The yield on 10 year T-bonds closed at 7.43 percent, down 0.05 percentage points from Tuesday's close.

The Australian dollar sagged back to support Wednesday as a painstakingly constructed rally above US$0.7950 proved to be built on sand. By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the dollar had retreated to US$0.7922/27 from an early US$0.7958/63 and an offshore peak of US$0.7970.
Short-term range Support Restnce RSI-14 MA-10 MA-20
Industrial leaders bounced back with Dow rebound.
Bellwether ended nearly unchanged after copper rally lent support early.
Major miner felt pressure from slide in U.K.-based sister entity RTZ Corp Plc.
Gold/nickel miner firmed in line with stronger base metals.
Beverage group's shares continue to be marked down a month
after its profit downgrade and following a cooler than usual
start to the Australian summer, dealers said.
